mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior quarter is interpreted by market participants as a signal of tightening financial conditions, which compresses discount rates and reduces the present value of future earnings for equities, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.5 percentage points over the past quarter
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: No significant correlation (p > 0.1) between 20-day SPX returns and the combined PAYEMS/UNRATE interaction in a rolling regression window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a sustained increase in retail sales (implied via HOUST) indicates expanding economic activity, which anticipates a positive business outlook and prompts traders to buy into S&P 500 futures, yielding positive 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >3% in the current month and HOUST increases by >1% in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day SPX returns are not statistically different from zero when regressed on the INDPRO-HOUST lead-lag configuration (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) over two consecutive months signals weakening demand and price pressures easing, which reduces growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months and CPIAUCSL falls by >1% in the second month
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are positively correlated with INDPRO-CPIAUCSL interaction (p < 0.05), contradicting the predicted negative relationship.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly rate of change in the federal funds rate turns positive (i.e., rates are rising), it indicates a shift toward tighter monetary policy, which raises the real discount rate and reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: first difference of FEDFUNDS is positive
failure_condition: 60-day SPX forward returns are not significantly different from zero when regressed on the FEDFUNDS first difference (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in labor force participation (implied via PAYEMS), suggests a tight labor market that drives wage growth and boosts corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are not positively correlated with the 3-month UNRATE staying below 4% (p > 0.05 in a rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail activity (HOUST) followed by a sustained rise in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates accelerating demand and cost pressures, which can trigger preemptive equity sell-off as investors price in higher future rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% in the current month and CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day SPX returns show no significant negative relationship with the HOUST-CPIAUCSL interaction (p > 0.1 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) combined with stable industrial production (INDPRO), market participants anticipate deflationary pressure and reduced corporate investment, which leads to downward revisions in growth forecasts and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.3% in the current month while INDPRO remains flat or slightly declining
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are positively correlated with the CPIAUCSL-INDPRO interaction (p < 0.05), contradicting the predicted negative relationship.
